title: Indefinite integrals
examples: How do I know when to use the constant C?
Is finding the integral always the reverse of the derivative?
What is the integral of x squared plus one?

explain.say: Today we are learning about indefinite integrals. This process is really the reverse of differentiation. Differentiation finds the rate of change. Integration finds the original function.

When we integrate a function, we must always add a constant C. This is the constant of integration. We add C because the derivative of any constant is zero. For example, the derivative of x squared plus five is two x. The derivative of x squared minus ten is also two x. We lose information about the original constant.

items: Must always add a constant C
Derivative of any constant is zero

explain.say: Let us look at a concrete example together. If we integrate two x, we get x squared. But remember to add C. So the integral of two x is x squared plus C. This accounts for the missing constant.

Another standard integral to remember is for x squared. The integral of x squared is one divided by three times x cubed. We use the power rule for this. The integral of x to the power of three is one fourth times x to the power of four plus C.

faq.q: Do I always have to add the constant C?
faq.a: Yes, you must always add the constant C. This represents any constant that was there originally but disappeared when you differentiated. You can also ask, 'Why do I need the constant C?' or 'What is the constant of integration?'
asks: What is the constant of integration?

faq.a: Yes, that is exactly what it is. Integration is the process of finding the antiderivative. You can also ask, 'What is the reverse process of calculus?' or 'How do I reverse the derivative?'
asks: What is the reverse process of calculus?
How do I reverse the derivative?

faq.q: What is the integral of a constant number like five?
faq.a: The integral of any constant number is that number times x. So the integral of five is five x plus C. You might also ask, 'What is the integral of 7?' or 'Integrate 5.'
asks: What is the integral of a constant?

faq.q: Can I use the power rule for integrals?
faq.a: Yes, you use the power rule just like with differentiation. If you integrate x to the power of n, you get (one divided by n plus one) times x to the power of n plus one, all over n plus one. You could also ask, 'How does the power rule work for integrals?'
asks: How does the power rule work for integrals?
Can I use the power rule?

faq.q: What is the integral of x squared?
faq.a: The integral of x squared is one divided by three times x cubed plus C. You could also ask, 'Integrate x².' or 'Find the integral of x squared.'
asks: Find the integral of x squared.
What is the integral of x squared?

facts: Indefinite integration is the process of finding the antiderivative.
The constant of integration, C, must always be included in an indefinite integral.
The power rule for integration states that the integral of x to the power of n is (one divided by n plus one) times x to the power of n plus one, divided by n plus one.
The integral of x is one half x squared plus C.

quiz.say: What is the indefinite integral of three x squared?
quiz.why: We use the power rule: three times (x to the power of three divided by three) plus C, which simplifies to x cubed plus C.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to divide by the new exponent, three.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly applies the derivative rule instead of the integral rule.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly places the division by three.

quiz.say: Find the integral of five x minus two.
quiz.why: We integrate term by term. The integral of five x is five times (x squared divided by two) plus C, and the integral of minus two is minus two x plus C.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to divide the first term by two.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly treats the constant term as not needing an x.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly applies the power rule to the constant term.

quiz.say: If the derivative is 4x plus 1, what is the original function?
quiz.why: We integrate 4x, which gives two x squared plus C, and we integrate one, which gives x plus C. Combining them gives two x squared plus x plus C.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to divide the first term by two.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly integrates the constant term one as one.
wrong.2: This mistake assumes the integral is the same as the original function.
